question: How should an explainer treat a position that will later be refuted?
premises: Any point that enters the explanation must be addressed.
Even a position to be refuted later should be stated strongly.
Firm reasoning should be used in presenting it.
inference: A fair explanation strengthens even the opposing position before refuting it later.
plain_english: Whatever point comes up in the explanation should be supported with very firm reasoning, even if it is something that will later be refuted.
